# v0.33.0

## Highlights

This release features 927 commits from 389 contributors (122 new)!

* **New models**: Reflection Beam-1.0 (501B MoE, 23B active) with its DFlash2 drafter (#62074), Yandex AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B (#57963), Recursive Flint (40B MoE, 2.5B active) (#62938), Muse Spark Open (#61879), Step-5 Preview (#61727, #63147), NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Super (#62957), Nemotron-Labs Dory1.0-4B (#60149), Nemotron Parse 3.5 (#61651), MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 (#63095), Domyn Edge (#62544) and the ColUltraVBERT visual document retriever (#62237).
* **PyTorch 2.14**: vLLM is upgraded to PyTorch 2.14.0, with torchvision 0.29.0 and Triton 3.8.0 (#52183).
* **CUDA 12.9 dropped**: release wheels and images are CUDA 13.0 only. The CUDA 12.9 wheels and the `-cu129` / `-cu129-ubuntu2404` images are no longer published (#62575); use the default CUDA 13.0 artifacts instead.
* **libtorch ABI stable CUDA wheel**: the CUDA wheel is now ABI stable with libtorch.
* **AWS EFA image**: a new `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.33.0-efa` image (x86_64 and aarch64) bundles the AWS EFA libraries and the EFA build of the Mooncake transfer engine, for KV transfer and multi-node serving on EFA-enabled EC2 instances (#58768).
* **`vllm/vllm` image alias**: every release image is now also published under the shorter `vllm/vllm` name, e.g. `vllm/vllm:v0.33.0`, `vllm/vllm:v0.33.0-efa` and `vllm/vllm:v0.33.0-rocm`.
* **Speculative decoding**: the new XPress refiner for block-diffusion drafters such as DFlash and DSpark (#54448); FLy, an opt-in lossy verification policy with 1.04-1.31x decode throughput on MI355X and B300 (#53987); DFlash/DSpark no longer reserve draft slots in the token budget, taking DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark on GB300 from 1373 to 3390 output tok/s in the PR's benchmark (#59468); quantized draft `lm_head` (`draft_lm_head_quantization`, +18% decode at concurrency 1) (#59973); lookahead block hashes so EAGLE/MTP prefix-cache hits keep their last block, on by default (#61589); and MTP drafts in the Transformers modeling backend (#61270).
* **Faster decode on NVIDIA**: opt-in latency-specialized decode on GB300 for Kimi-K3 (1.5-2x at TP8/TP16, #61867) and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (18.3% faster decode step at batch 1, #61868); DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 MXFP4 experts run as block FP8 through Humming on Hopper (+9-21% decode on 4x H200, #61875); FA4 sparse MLA decode on Blackwell (#55866); FlashInfer DCP prefill on trtllm-gen with 39-48% lower mean TTFT at 100k input on 8xB200 (#62029); and decode-only full CUDA graphs under MRV2 prefill context parallelism (2.6x over eager, #62377).
* **AMD ROCm**: the default ROCm image and wheels move to ROCm 10.0, with ROCm 7.2 still published as `-rocm72` (#58761); MonoKernel decode via `--monokernel` for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI300X/MI325X (2.32x P50 interactivity at concurrency 1, #60731) and on every MI355X layer (#61082), and for MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 on MI355X (16.6% lower TPOT, #62712, #62994); the `ROCM_OCTAVE` 3-4 bit KV cache (4.6x the KV tokens of fp16 on RX 7900 XTX, #59774); and gfx1250 enablement for gpt-oss-120b, DeepSeek-R1, DeepSeek-V4-Flash and MiniMax-M3 (#58800).
* **API and serving**: the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/decisions` endpoint, on by default for supported generation models (#60465, #61550); token embeddings with optional late chunking on `/v1/embeddings` (#61772, #63051, #60164); `output_mode="derender"` on `/inference/v1/generate` (#60082); a large Rust frontend parity push, including no more HTTP 500 on long conversations (#62374) and unsupported flags failing at startup (#62431); concurrent worker startup with TP > 1 (#60028); and a watchdog that dumps stack traces from stuck engine and worker processes (#55700).
* **Breaking changes**: Medusa and the MLP speculator removed (#61701); the legacy Ray compiled-graph executor removed (#61712, #62228); `--mamba-cache-mode` deprecated (#60043); requests sent while generation is paused now get HTTP 503 (#51488); the NIXL connector needs NIXL 1.5 or newer (#61032); LM Format Enforcer and `--ir-op-priority` deprecated (#63423, #63371).

## Release Artifacts

<!-- TODO: verify every URL and tag after publishing (wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/0.33.0/, wheels.vllm.ai/0.33.0/xpu, Docker Hub tags, GitHub release assets). -->

### Python Wheels

| Platform | Install |
|---|---|
| PyPI (CUDA 13.0) | `pip install vllm` |
| PyPI (CUDA 13.0, uv) | `uv pip install vllm --torch-backend=auto` |
| ROCm 10.0 | `pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/0.33.0/rocm100` |
| ROCm 7.2 | `pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/0.33.0/rocm72` |
| XPU | `uv pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/0.33.0/xpu --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/xpu --index-strategy unsafe-best-match` |

### Docker Images

| Platform | Docker Image |
|---|---|
| CUDA 13.0 (Default) | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:v0.33.0` |
| CUDA 13.0 + AWS EFA | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:v0.33.0-efa` |
| ROCm 10.0 | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.33.0` |
| ROCm 7.2 | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.33.0-rocm72` |
| CPU | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:v0.33.0` |
| XPU | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:v0.33.0` |

Every image is also available under the shorter `vllm/vllm` name: `vllm/vllm:v0.33.0`, `vllm/vllm:v0.33.0-efa`, `vllm/vllm:v0.33.0-rocm` (`-rocm100`, `-rocm72`), `vllm/vllm:v0.33.0-cpu` and `vllm/vllm:v0.33.0-xpu`. `latest` works the same way, e.g. `vllm/vllm:latest-rocm`.

### Other Artifacts

Pre-built release artifacts are available in the **Assets** section at the bottom of this page, including:
- Source distribution tarball
- CUDA 13.0 Python wheels for x86_64 and arm64
- CPU Python wheels for x86_64, arm64, and macOS
- XPU Python wheel for x86_64

## Model Support
* **New models**: Reflection Beam-1.0 (`BeamForCausalLM`) day-0 support with its DFlash2 drafter and fused Blackwell kernels (#62074, #62042), plus `beam` reasoning and tool parsers (#62052); Yandex AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B (Kimi Delta Attention hybrid, 512-expert MoE, 262K context) (#57963); Recursive Flint BF16 and NVFP4 GGUF checkpoints with small-batch Blackwell decode kernels (#62938); Muse Spark Open (#61879) with reasoning and tool parsers (#62207); Step-5 Preview (#61727, #62126, #62132), running on SM100 (#63147) with LoRA (#62498); NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Super (#62957); Nemotron-Labs Dory1.0-4B (#60149); Nemotron Parse 3.5 with an MTP proposer on MRV2 (#61651); MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 (#63095); Domyn Edge (#62544); ColUltraVBERT (#62237); LFM2.5-Embedding-350M (`Lfm2BidirectionalModel`, #62201); Kolibri 1 through the Transformers backend (#60827); and Decision 3.0 models (#61565, #61778) and Cloudflare Clef-Flash (#61308) on `/v1/systemone`.
* **DeepSeek-V4 and V4.1**: length-aware decode indexer block selection (about 850 us saved per step at 1M context, #61039); MegaMoE experts loaded directly in the DeepGEMM layout so `reload_weights` works (#60096); `fused_wqa_wkv` split by token across TP on SM90 (#58872); MegaAttn `wo_a` writes MXFP8 input for `wo_b` (#60118); native small-head FlashMLA sparse prefill on SM90 (#61615); FlashMLA interleaved KV layout (#61371); redundant EPLB expert slots loaded (#59611); GPU Engram tables read from peer HBM, fixing DEP decode hangs on GB200 (#62091); and fixes for Engram under PP (#62208), Engram all-to-all hangs (#62269), prefill index-workspace NaNs (#60613), C128 compressed-KV writes under PIECEWISE graphs (#59709), routed-expert rows under replay (#61643, #62652) and the updated 1017 reference encoding (#62199, #62200).
* **GLM**: GLM-5.3-Flash defaults to an FP8 KV cache (9.8% higher end-to-end throughput in the PR's benchmark, #61228) and gets mHC TileLang decode kernels on Blackwell (#62745); GLM-5.3 per-token-group quant (2.8% ITL, #60927), in-place draft decode metadata (#61873) and skipped `concat_and_cache_mla` scales (1.2-3.0% TPOT on B300, #62102); FP8 indexer WK pairs kept across `load_weights` calls, fixing thinking loops with runai_streamer (#59223).
* **Kimi-K3**: KDA RecoverSSM CuTe DSL verify/commit kernels on SM10x, with verify records moved out of the KV cache so KV connectors work (#63045); online quantization of NVIDIA projections (#62980).
* **Qwen**: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next FP8 QSA KV cache on Ampere (#60602, #60992), packed NVFP4 PLE embeddings that fit Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 on one DGX Spark (#56273) and PLE short-conv prefill checkpoints (#61601); FlashInfer GDN prefill checkpoints for Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5 (#60050).
* **Other models**: Cohere2MoE attention/MoE dual stream, single TP all-reduce and fused add + RMSNorm (1.14-1.36x TPOT, on by default, #62101); Beam TP all-reduce fused with norms and MoE finalize (#62366); MiniMax-M3 CUTLASS MSA decode crossover (#55838); Granite MoE as an EAGLE3/DFlash/DSpark target (#61110); NemotronHMTP sharing target embeddings (#62194); LoRA for BERT cross-encoders and token classification (#61279, #61391).
* **Multimodal**: PaddleOCR-VL batched vision encoder (34-85% more throughput, #61458) and `compile_mm_encoder` (#61838); DeepSeek-VL2 ViT full CUDA graphs (#46005); Gemma4Unified batched embedding (#60643); Pixtral real-valued RoPE under compile (#63145); and fixes for EXAONE-4.5 images (broken since v0.29.0, #61104), Gemma 4 encoder graphs (#61365, #60687, #63538), DeepSeek-VL2 encoder cache and PP (#63120, #63192) and Gemma 4 placeholders (#61196).
* **Transformers modeling backend**: MTP speculative drafts (#61270), fused post-top-k MoE routers (#57410), graph caching instead of AOT caching (#58918) and dynamic-RoPE CUDA graphs (#58064).

## Engine Core

## Breaking Changes & Deprecations
* CUDA 12.9 wheels and images are no longer published (#62575).
* Medusa and the MLP speculator were removed (#61701). The legacy Ray compiled-graph executor was removed and `VLLM_USE_RAY_V2_EXECUTOR_BACKEND` is gone; `RayExecutorV2` is the only Ray executor (#61712, #62228).
* Deprecated: `--mamba-cache-mode` (no effect, #60043), `--ir-op-priority` (removal in v0.34.0, #63371), and the LM Format Enforcer structured-output backend (opt-in in v0.34.0, removal in v0.35.0, #63423).
* API changes: requests sent while generation is paused return HTTP 503 (#51488); `kv_transfer_params` / `ec_transfer_params` moved to the top level of render output (#61241); LoRA on a model without LoRA support fails at validation (#61884); the RL weight-transfer API now uses `ParamMeta`, `iter_full()` and `iter_local()` (#63256); beam search scores are normalized by generated length (#62928).
* Rust frontend: unsupported `vllm serve` flags and request fields fail instead of being ignored (#62431, #62434); request-supplied chat templates need `--trust-request-chat-template` (#62673); an empty `tools` array returns 400 (#63060).
* The NIXL connector requires NIXL 1.5 or newer (#61032).
* Removed env vars: `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY` (#61628), `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM` (#61278) and `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MEGA_MOE_FUSE_SHARED_EXPERTS` (#61345); `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE` is replaced by `--monokernel` (#61082).
* New defaults: GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 KV cache (#61228); lookahead block hashes for EAGLE/MTP prefix caching (#61589); Cohere2MoE dual stream (#62101); FA4 sparse MLA decode at 16 or fewer query heads per rank on Blackwell (#55866); ROCm: AITER FP8/FP4 BMM for MLA off (#53123), FlyDSL GDN prefill (#60645), AITER `topk_gating` (#56226), `rms_norm_gated` (#60250) and MXFP4 indexer K cache on CDNA4 for DeepSeek-V4 (#63669).

Open source · MIT · runs on your computer, model of your choice

An open-source coding agent for your terminal, desktop, browser and editor.

It reads your project, edits files and runs commands and tests. Have it ask before each step, or work on its own within limits you set. Files its edit tools changed can be rewound. New here? Start with the Studio desktop app.

Maintained by Huahui Yu.

> [!IMPORTANT] > **Community · 加入社区** — bilingual Discord for setup help (`#help` / `#求助`), workflow showcases, and feature ideas. → **** > > QQ group **DeepSeek-Reasonix官方群** (`1093562660`) → **** ([QR code](./docs/assets/qq-group.svg)) > Douyin: **做游戏的小鱼** (Douyin ID `22703872788`) · [QR code](./docs/assets/douyin.png)
## ❤️Sponsor
Thanks to Right Code for sponsoring this project! Right Code reliably provides routing services for models such as Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini, with both pay-as-you-go and monthly subscription billing options available. Invoices are available upon top-up, and enterprise and team users can receive dedicated one-on-one support. Register via this link.
Thanks to PackyCode for sponsoring this project! Access leading AI models through PackyCode with one API endpoint and one API key, with automatic failover and dedicated high-speed routes for Codex and Claude Code. Register via this link.
## What it is Reasonix is an open-source AI coding assistant. The program runs on your computer; the AI model is a service you configure, which receives what it reads. You describe a task in plain language; it reads code, edits files and runs commands and tests inside the project folder you choose, and shows you each step. You pick the model: a DeepSeek preset is built in, any OpenAI-compatible service is one config entry, and you pay the model provider directly. ## What you get - **Read, edit, run.** It reads code, edits files and runs tests and commands, all inside your project folder. - **Permission levels.** Have it ask every time, or let everyday actions run on their own; your forbid rules always hold. To see the approach first, use plan mode: it starts work only once you approve. - **Rewind.** A file is saved before it changes, so you can rewind by conversation turn without touching your git history. Only files its edit tools changed are covered, not what a shell command did. ## 30-second start Download, add a model key, open a project. New here? Start with the Studio desktop app. 1. Download and install the desktop app, Reasonix Studio, from the [releases page](https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/releases?q=studio-v&expanded=true). 2. Open it and enter your model provider and key when asked. 3. Open your project folder and write what you want, for example "add retry on failure to the http client". 4. At the level you chose, it stops and asks before anything that needs your say-so. Allow it to continue, or refuse. Prefer a terminal? Download the `reasonix` command-line tool, run `reasonix setup` to pick a model, then run `reasonix`. See [Install](#install) and [Quick start](#quick-start). ## Four ways to use it - **Desktop app (Studio).** A graphical app; the best place to start. - **Terminal.** A full-screen text interface; `reasonix run "task"` also works in scripts. - **Browser.** `reasonix web` opens a web interface on your own machine. - **Editor.** Install the extension in VS Code; other editors that support ACP (Agent Client Protocol, a common way for an editor to connect to an AI assistant) can connect to `reasonix acp`. All four are the same program underneath. What follows is for advanced users and contributors. ## Use it from DeepSeek Harness DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) can hand a task to Reasonix as a subagent over ACP. This repository publishes a plugin index for it: 1. Run `reasonix setup` on the machine that runs `dsh`. In the DSH Web UI turn on Custom plugin markets (Plugins, More) and add this index in the Discover tab: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/studio/integrations/dsh-plugin/market-index.json` 2. Install "Reasonix subagent" from it. 3. Open the plugin's page and turn its switch on. While it is off the model has no `reasonix` tool and may run `reasonix -p` in its own shell, which looks like a delegation and is not one. Setup details, the permission policy and limits are in [Using Reasonix from DeepSeek Harness](./docs/DSH.md). ## Versions Reasonix ships on two lines. See the [version roadmap announcement](https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/discussions/10748) for the reasoning behind the split. | Line | Branch | Status | Get it | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Reasonix 2.x** | `studio` (this branch) | Active development | [Studio releases](https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/releases?q=studio-v&expanded=true) | | **Reasonix 1.x** | [`main-v2`](https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/tree/main-v2) | Maintenance / stable | `npm i -g reasonix` · [desktop download](https://reasonix.io/?download=desktop#start) | - **Want something stable?** Stay on 1.x. It keeps receiving bug fixes, provider/API compatibility, updater and security fixes; its core architecture is no longer being extended. - **Want the new architecture?** Use 2.x Reasonix Studio. It is still moving quickly; reports are welcome. Valuable fixes, tests and behaviour from 1.x are reviewed one by one and ported or reimplemented on 2.x where they fit the new architecture. - [Moving from 1.x to 2.x](./docs/MIGRATING.md): what the two lines share, and how to run both on one machine without losing sessions. - [2.x roadmap](./docs/ROADMAP.md): what 2.x still has to deliver, how it ships, and the decisions still open. ## Features Technical highlights for advanced users. - **Config-driven.** Providers, the agent, enabled tools, and plugins are all declared in `reasonix.toml`. No hardcoded models. - **Multi-model & composable.** DeepSeek ships as a preset; any OpenAI-compatible endpoint is a config entry, not new code. Optionally run two models together (executor + planner) in separate, cache-stable sessions. - **Plugin-driven.** MCP servers contribute tools, prompts, and resources; Extension Protocol v1 sidecars can also intercept runtime events, contribute Providers and structured UI, and ship versioned plugin packages. - **Cache-aware context maintenance.** Startup injects a small stable environment summary, stale tool output is snipped/pruned before summary compaction, and the built-in tool schema contract is documented for regression review. - **Zero-friction distribution.** `CGO_ENABLED=0` single binary; cross-compile to six targets with one command. The result is a fully self-contained static binary — nothing to install on the target machine beyond the binary itself. ## Install This branch is **Reasonix 2.x**. Its desktop app is Reasonix Studio; the CLI, Studio, and editor integrations all run the same local Reasonix engine. ### Reasonix Studio (2.x) Download the package for your platform from the latest [Studio release](https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/releases?q=studio-v&expanded=true) (tagged `studio-v2.*`; candidates such as `-rc.N` are marked as pre-releases): | Platform | Package | Architecture | | --- | --- | --- | | macOS | `.dmg` or `.zip` | Apple Silicon (`arm64`) / Intel (`amd64`) | | Windows | Installer `-installer.exe` or portable `.zip` | x64 | | Linux | `.deb`, `.rpm`, or `.AppImage` (download only) | x64 (`amd64`) / ARM64 (`arm64`, aarch64) | Every package ships with a `.minisig` signature, and the release carries `SHA256SUMS`. Once installed, Studio updates itself in place. The same release also carries the 2.x `reasonix` CLI as archives for `darwin|linux|windows × amd64|arm64`. The Android build ships on that release as `ReasonixMobile-.apk` (`arm64`, Android 8.0 or newer). The kernel and the page run on the phone, and the agent reaches your servers over SSH; pairing with a computer is done by scanning the code it shows. The APK is signed with the Android release key rather than minisign, so it carries a `.sha256` and no `.minisig`. When that key is absent the build is named `ReasonixMobile--unsigned.apk`. Android refuses to install an unsigned package, so those builds stay a workflow artifact for whoever wants to sign one, and the release carries no APK at all. ### Reasonix 1.x (stable) The 1.x CLI installs through npm on any supported platform, or Homebrew on macOS: ```sh npm i -g reasonix # any OS; pulls the prebuilt native binary brew install esengine/reasonix/reasonix # macOS ``` The 1.x desktop app is on the [official download page](https://reasonix.io/?download=desktop#start). Windows installers are code-signed with a Certum code-signing certificate. ### VS Code extension The extension does not bundle the CLI; it starts your local `reasonix acp` backend and adds native chat, editor context, tool-call approvals, model selection, and workspace sessions. Install the 1.x CLI first. - **VS Code:** [install from Visual Studio Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=SivanLiu.reasonix-agent) - **VSCodium / Eclipse Theia:** [install from Open VSX Registry](https://open-vsx.org/extension/SivanLiu/reasonix-agent) - **Extension ID:** `SivanLiu.reasonix-agent` · [source and usage guide](https://github.com/SivanCola/reasonix-vscode) ### Build from source Clone the repository; `studio` builds 2.x and `main-v2` builds 1.x: ```sh git clone https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix.git cd DeepSeek-Reasonix git switch studio ``` #### CLI The CLI build requires **Go 1.25+**. The module pins a `toolchain` directive; keep `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto` so Go downloads the pinned toolchain, or install it. ```sh make build # -> bin/reasonix(.exe) make cross # -> dist/ (darwin|linux|windows × amd64|arm64) ``` #### Studio Studio additionally requires **Node 24+ and pnpm 10** (`npm install -g pnpm@10`) for the frontend. ```sh make studio ``` See the [Studio build guide](desktop/README.md#prerequisites) for platform webview dependencies and Linux build tags. ## Quick start ### Reasonix Studio Install and launch Studio, then connect a provider and model in the app. No CLI setup is needed. ### CLI / TUI ```sh reasonix setup # configure a provider and model reasonix # start an interactive session reasonix run "implement the TODOs in main.go" ``` In an interactive session, run `/init` when you want Reasonix to create project instructions. For advanced CLI usage and configuration, see the **[CLI reference](./docs/CLI.md)**, **[Guide](./docs/GUIDE.md)**, and **[configuration paths](./docs/CONFIG_PATHS.md)**. ## Documentation - **Getting started:** [Guide](./docs/GUIDE.md) · [CLI reference](./docs/CLI.md) · [Configuration paths](./docs/CONFIG_PATHS.md) · [ACP editor integration](./docs/ACP.md) · [Use from DeepSeek Harness](./docs/DSH.md) - **Features & troubleshooting:** [Subagent profiles](./docs/SUBAGENT_PROFILES.md) · [Context Engine v2](./docs/SESSION_MEMORY_RETRIEVAL.md) · [Capability diagnostics](./docs/CAPABILITY_DIAGNOSTICS.md) · [Recovery and updates](./docs/RECOVERY.md) · [Checkpoints & rewind](./docs/CHECKPOINTS.md) - **Agent presets:** [Session Agent compositions](./docs/AGENT_COMPOSITIONS.md) - **Engineering & migration:** [Spec](./docs/SPEC.md) · [Task contracts & pause policy](./docs/TASK_CONTRACT.md) · [Tool contract](./docs/TOOL_CONTRACT.md) · [Moving from 1.x to 2.x](./docs/MIGRATING.md) · [2.x roadmap](./docs/ROADMAP.md) - **Extension development:** [Skills](./docs/SKILLS.md) · [Extensions](./docs/EXTENSIONS.md) · [Plugin packages and Manifest v1](./docs/PLUGIN_PACKAGES.md) · [Extension Protocol](./docs/EXTENSION_PROTOCOL.md) · [Go SDK and starter](./sdk/go/README.md) ## Star History

latestRelease.body:
本版新增工作台里的 Word 和 Excel 只读预览；修复 `serve` 密码出现在进程命令行里的问题，并改进长时间等待后台任务时模型的表现和功耗。

## 新增

- 工作台可只读预览 Word（.docx）和 Excel（.xlsx），含多工作表、数字格式和合并单元格；在隔离框中显示、不运行宏和脚本，可在设置里关闭。关联 #14622。

## 修复

- 安全：`reasonix serve` 新增 `--password-file`，密码从仅所有者可读的文件读取，不再出现在进程命令行里；`--hash-password` 同样支持。修复 #14913 fixed in #14914。
- 让模型盯后台长任务（如打包）时，它不再轮询几次就写「未完成」收尾；工具结果会告诉它任务结束后会自动开一轮继续。修复 #14879 fixed in #14900。
- 视觉效果设为「节能」后，运行中的循环动画（状态标志描线、会话行流光、工具旋转图标）也会停下，长时间等待任务时不再让显卡持续工作。修复 #14919 fixed in #14922。
- 运行中发送带技能卡片的消息时，按钮和提示如实显示「排队发送」，不再写着「插话」却悄悄排队。关联 #14889。
- 重启后出现在待发送区、需要你决定的后台任务完成通知，标签写明「后台 · 状态不明」或「后台 · 受阻」，不再和你自己发的消息混在一起。关联 #14885。
- 文件大小在进位时显示为下一单位（如 1024 KB 显示为 1.0 MB）。关联 #14890 by @kevin9327。
- 浏览器脚本结果、电脑操控拒绝原因、插件启动失败摘要等处截断的中文不再出现半个字符。关联 #14891 by @kevin9327、#14894 by @kevin9327、#14907 by @kevin9327、#14908 by @kevin9327、#14911 by @kevin9327、#14912 by @kevin9327。

## 贡献者

感谢本版本的贡献者：@kevin9327

---

<!-- lang:en -->

## New

- The workbench previews Word (.docx) and Excel (.xlsx) read-only in an isolated frame with no macros or scripts; it can be turned off in Settings. Refs #14622.

## Fixed

- Security: `reasonix serve` takes `--password-file`, reading the password from an owner-only file instead of argv where `ps` shows it; `--hash-password` accepts it too. Fixes #14913 fixed in #14914.
- A model watching a long background job such as a build no longer gives up and reports it unfinished; it is told a new turn starts when the job ends. Fixes #14879 fixed in #14900.
- Reduced visual effects now also stop the looping run animations (status mark, session-row sweep, tool spinner), so a long wait no longer keeps the GPU busy. Fixes #14919 fixed in #14922.
- While a turn runs, a message with a skill card shows "Queue" on the button and hint instead of "Steer", since steering carries plain text only. Refs #14889.
- A background job's follow-on that needs a decision in the pending panel is labelled "Background · uncertain" or "Background · blocked", apart from your own lines. Refs #14885.
- Byte sizes move to the next unit when rounding carries over: 1024 KB shows as 1.0 MB. Refs #14890 by @kevin9327.
- Multi-byte text cut in browser results, computer refusals and plugin failure summaries no longer ends in half a character. Refs #14891 by @kevin9327, #14894 by @kevin9327, #14907 by @kevin9327, #14908 by @kevin9327, #14911 by @kevin9327, #14912 by @kevin9327.

## Contributors

Thanks to this release's contributors: @kevin9327

## What's Changed
* fix(size): move byte sizes to the next unit when rounding reaches 1024 by @kevin9327 in https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/pull/14890
* fix(capability): cut semantic-router candidate descriptions on a rune boundary by @kevin9327 in https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/pull/14891
* fix(composer): name a running send with a skill card as queued by @esengine in https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/pull/14893
* fix(plugin): cut MCP startup failure summaries on a rune boundary by @kevin9327 in https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/pull/14894
* fix(queue): label a background job's follow-on that needs a decision as background by @esengine in https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix/pull/14898

repo.readme: # OpenAI Agents SDK [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/openai-agents?label=pypi%20package)](https://pypi.org/project/openai-agents/) The OpenAI Agents SDK is a lightweight yet powerful framework for building multi-agent workflows. It is provider-agnostic, supporting the OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions APIs, as well as 100+ other LLMs. > [!NOTE] > Looking for the JavaScript/TypeScript version? Check out [Agents SDK JS/TS](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-js). ### Core concepts: 1. [**Agents**](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/agents): LLMs configured with instructions, tools, guardrails, and handoffs 1. [**Sandbox agents**](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/sandbox_agents): Agents preconfigured to work with a container to perform work over long time horizons. 1. [**Realtime agents**](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/realtime/quickstart/): Build powerful voice agents with `gpt-realtime-2.1` and full agent features 1. [**Voice agents**](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/voice/quickstart/): Build voice pipelines that combine speech-to-text, an agent workflow, and text-to-speech 1. **[Agents as tools](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/tools/#agents-as-tools) / [Handoffs](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/handoffs/)**: Delegating to other agents for specific tasks 1. [**Tools**](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/tools/): Various Tools let agents take actions (functions, MCP, hosted tools) 1. [**Guardrails**](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/guardrails/): Configurable safety checks for input and output validation 1. [**Human in the loop**](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/human_in_the_loop/): Built-in mechanisms for involving humans across agent runs 1. [**Sessions**](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/sessions/): Automatic conversation history management across agent runs 1. [**Tracing**](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/tracing/): Built-in tracking of agent runs, allowing you to view, debug and optimize your workflows Explore the [examples](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/tree/main/examples) directory to see the SDK in action, and read our [documentation](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/) for more details. ## Get started To get started, set up your Python environment (Python 3.10 or newer required), and then install OpenAI Agents SDK package. ### venv ```bash python -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate # On Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate pip install openai-agents ``` For voice support, install with the optional `voice` group: `pip install 'openai-agents[voice]'`. For Redis session support, install with the optional `redis` group: `pip install 'openai-agents[redis]'`. ### uv If you're familiar with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), installing the package would be even easier: ```bash uv init uv add openai-agents ``` For voice support, install with the optional `voice` group: `uv add 'openai-agents[voice]'`. For Redis session support, install with the optional `redis` group: `uv add 'openai-agents[redis]'`. ## Run your first agents The SDK supports four primary ways to run agents. Set the `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variable before running any of these examples. ### Run a text agent Use a text `Agent` for workflows that do not need a persistent realtime connection or a sandbox workspace. ```python from agents import Agent, Runner agent = Agent(name="Assistant", instructions="You are a helpful assistant") result = Runner.run_sync(agent, "Write a haiku about recursion in programming.") print(result.final_output) # Code within the code, # Functions calling themselves, # Infinite loop's dance. ``` (_For Jupyter notebook users, see [hello_world_jupyter.ipynb](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/examples/basic/hello_world_jupyter.ipynb)_) ### Run a sandbox agent Use a [`SandboxAgent`](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/sandbox_agents) when the agent needs to inspect files, run commands, apply patches, or preserve workspace state across longer tasks. This example uses `UnixLocalSandboxClient`, which is supported on macOS and Linux. On Windows, use `DockerSandboxClient` with the `openai-agents[docker]` extra or a hosted sandbox client instead; see [Sandbox clients](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/sandbox/clients/) for setup details. ```python from agents import Runner from agents.run import RunConfig from agents.sandbox import Manifest, SandboxAgent, SandboxRunConfig from agents.sandbox.entries import GitRepo from agents.sandbox.sandboxes import UnixLocalSandboxClient agent = SandboxAgent( name="Workspace Assistant", instructions="Inspect the sandbox workspace before answering.", default_manifest=Manifest( entries={"repo": GitRepo(repo="openai/openai-agents-python", ref="main")} ), ) result = Runner.run_sync( agent, "Inspect the repo README and summarize what this project does.", run_config=RunConfig(sandbox=SandboxRunConfig(client=UnixLocalSandboxClient())), ) print(result.final_output) ``` ### Run a realtime agent Use a [`RealtimeAgent`](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/realtime/quickstart/) for low-latency, server-side voice and multimodal experiences over WebSocket. ```python import asyncio from agents.realtime import RealtimeAgent, RealtimeRunner async def main() -> None: agent = RealtimeAgent( name="Assistant", instructions="You are a helpful voice assistant. Keep responses short." ) runner = RealtimeRunner(starting_agent=agent) session = await runner.run() async with session: await session.send_message("Say hello in one short sentence.") async for event in session: if event.type == "audio": # Forward or play event.audio.data. pass elif event.type == "history_added": print(event.item) elif event.type == "agent_end": break if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main()) ``` ### Run a voice agent Use a [`VoicePipeline`](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/voice/quickstart/) to turn audio into text, run an agent workflow, and stream generated speech. ```python import asyncio import numpy as np from agents import Agent from agents.voice import AudioInput, SingleAgentVoiceWorkflow, VoicePipeline async def main() -> None: agent = Agent(name="Assistant", instructions="You are a helpful voice assistant.") pipeline = VoicePipeline(workflow=SingleAgentVoiceWorkflow(agent)) audio_input = AudioInput(buffer=np.zeros(24000 * 3, dtype=np.int16)) result = await pipeline.run(audio_input) async for event in result.stream(): if event.type == "voice_stream_event_audio": # Forward or play event.data. pass if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main()) ``` Explore the [examples](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/tree/main/examples) directory to see the SDK in action, and read our [documentation](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/) for more details. ## Contributing Please share bug reports and feature requests through [GitHub issues](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/issues). Pull requests are limited to repository collaborators; we do not accept pull requests from non-collaborators. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for the contribution policy and development guide. For security vulnerabilities, follow [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/SECURITY.md). ## Acknowledgements We'd like to acknowledge the excellent work of the open-source community, especially: - [Pydantic](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/) - [Requests](https://github.com/psf/requests) - [MCP Python SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk) - [Griffe](https://github.com/mkdocstrings/griffe) This library has these optional dependencies: - [websockets](https://github.com/python-websockets/websockets) - [SQLAlchemy](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy) - [any-llm](https://github.com/mozilla-ai/any-llm) and [LiteLLM](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm) We also rely on the following tools to manage the project: - [uv](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv) and [ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff) - [mypy](https://github.com/python/mypy) and [Pyright](https://github.com/microsoft/pyright) - [pytest](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest) and [Coverage.py](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy) - [MkDocs](https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material) We're committed to continuing to build the Agents SDK as an open source framework so others in the community can expand on our approach.

- Minimum required release type: minor. Existing tool error formatters receive a new category, and the RunState reader restricts some legacy agent identities.
- Versioning verdict: compatible with the required minor release.

### Release call

**🟢 GREEN LIGHT TO SHIP.** The prepared 0.24.0 candidate has no unresolved release blocker. Its compatibility changes have supported migration or fallback paths described below.

### Scope summary

- 111 files changed (+15,444/-1,412). Main areas: tool execution and failure recovery, durable RunState and session history, sandbox safety, tracing, examples, dependencies, and release metadata.
- The candidate contains current main and #5335. Changes beyond main are limited to release-owned metadata.

### Risk assessment (ordered by impact)

1. **Route affected saved runs to their original SDK and agent code.**
   - Risk: **🟢 LOW**, with a required upgrade precaution. Some previously readable checkpoints now fail safely instead of risking incorrect agent ownership.
   - Evidence: the writer advances from schema 1.18 to 1.21. The reader rejects certain older graphs with same-name non-root agents whose saved identity ordering could have depended on hook attributes, even when those attributes remained unchanged. New identity generation excludes all hook instance attributes and retains the hook type. Graphs distinguishable only by those attributes cannot be serialized. Other supported historical schemas remain readable.
   - Files: `src/agents/run_state.py`, `src/agents/_run_state_agent_identity.py`, `tests/test_run_state.py`.
   - Action: finish affected legacy tasks with the original SDK, unchanged agent definitions, and hook ordering used when the snapshot was written. Use unique agent names before starting new durable runs. Do not rename a stored graph or change its schema label to force migration. Older SDKs cannot read new 1.21 snapshots.

2. **Update existing custom tool error formatters for a third category.**
   - Risk: **🟢 LOW**, with an explicit migration for exhaustive callbacks. A formatter that treats every non-rejection as a missing tool can now return misleading text for a crashed function.
   - Evidence: `ToolErrorFormatterArgs.kind` adds `"tool_exception"`; the optional `error` field is appended. The run-wide callback now handles eligible decorated function failures. Explicit per-tool handlers, including explicit `None` or the default handler, keep precedence. Factory-created MCP and `Agent.as_tool` failures, timeouts, cancellation, and schema-backed program calls keep their separate behavior.
   - Files: `src/agents/run_config.py`, `src/agents/tool.py`, `src/agents/run_internal/tool_execution.py`, `tests/test_tool_exception_formatter.py`.
   - Action: handle `"tool_exception"` explicitly or return `None` for it to retain the default message. Keep exception details out of model-visible output unless deliberately sanitized. With no custom formatter, default behavior stays unchanged.

3. **Preserve completed work without promising automatic replay.**
   - Risk: **🟢 LOW**. Recovery retains more completed work, but applications must still reconcile external side effects and partially committed history.
   - Evidence: deferred approval history waits for the output guardrail boundary. For client-managed runs, accepted call/output pairs survive sibling or callback failures after input and tool-output guardrails permit publication. Server-managed conversations retain their separate recovery path. Pending writes retain session identity and compaction state. Automatic compaction waits for pending approvals; standalone Redis replacement uses a transaction. Conversations writes use batches of at most 20 items and can commit partially across requests.
   - Files: `src/agents/run_internal/session_persistence.py`, `src/agents/run_internal/tool_execution.py`, `src/agents/memory/openai_conversations_session.py`, `src/agents/memory/openai_responses_compaction_session.py`, `src/agents/extensions/memory/redis_session.py`.
   - Action: resume supported nonterminal failures with the original session backend and ID, using returned state and history instead of replaying completed tools. After a partial Conversations append, inspect and repair remote history before retrying; do not resend the full list while an earlier part remains stored. Coordinate other writers; Redis atomic replacement does not prevent stale compaction across processes. Redis Cluster reads and pops remain available, but transactional append, clear, and replacement require a supported backend. Terminal output failures do not become replayable.

4. **Retain the intended sandbox, tracing, and display boundaries.**
   - Risk: **🟢 LOW**. macOS local commands can no longer launch host applications through Launch Services; disabled runs emit fewer spans inside caller-owned traces.
   - Evidence: #5335 adds Launch Services denial to the shared normal/PTY macOS profile. Native coverage checks the operating-system decision. Sandbox input validation returns recoverable tool errors without swallowing provider failures. Protected mount failures produce fresh redacted errors. Source arguments and linked exceptions remain intact, but the caught source traceback is detached. Tracing opt-out covers resumed tools and streamed cleanup, while resumed approved tools use the agent span. The realtime example renders tool content as literal text.
   - Files: `src/agents/sandbox/sandboxes/unix_local.py`, `src/agents/sandbox/_mount_security.py`, `src/agents/run.py`, `src/agents/tracing/`, `examples/realtime/app/static/app.js`.
   - Action: retain the macOS behavior note and #5335 reporter credit in the release. Do not describe local sandboxing as complete host or network isolation; use the documented Docker or hosted alternatives where needed. No tracing or realtime configuration migration is required.

5. **Keep additive integrations and dependency requirements explicit.**
   - Risk: **🟢 LOW**. Consumers opting into metadata, examples, or extras must use their specific contracts.
   - Evidence: converted MCP tools expose copied `mcp_annotations` metadata; it does not grant approval or become a model tool schema. Decisions examples use a separate OpenAI client with named typed answers and conservative refusal handling. Core Python support remains >=3.10 and the OpenAI dependency remains >=3.0.0,<4. The examples require OpenAI >=3.26.0,<4; the Temporal extra pins 1.34.0 and the Vercel extra accepts >=0.7.0,<0.9.
   - Files: `src/agents/mcp/util.py`, `src/agents/tool.py`, `examples/decisions/`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`.
   - Action: treat MCP annotations as untrusted discovery hints. Non-MCP and unannotated tools return `None`; reads return copies. Omitted hints stay omitted, so apply the installed MCP defaults yourself. The metadata is not serialized into tool origin. Install the example-specific SDK version and retain separate client/tracing ownership. Refresh application lockfiles when adopting the changed extras.

### Documentation coverage (non-blocking)

- Coverage source: current candidate documentation and a fresh search of all open PRs. The only open documentation PR is #5370 at `7754b11c7a8b4a2a0e9492f43de5f4762c456367`; its complete diff removes Runloop guidance for unmerged #5369. It does not cover this release's new obligations. Runloop removal is outside this candidate.
- Status: partially covered.
- Covered obligations: existing SDK/agent version routing for saved tasks; tracing opt-out and local sandbox limits; MCP callable approval policies; computer safety checks; Decisions example setup, separate client ownership, refusal handling, and routing limitations.
- Gaps and exact post-release suggestions:

| File and section | Wording or example to add |
| --- | --- |
| `docs/human_in_the_loop.md`, "Versioning pending tasks" and "Serialization options" | Explain schema 1.21, the legacy hook-identity restriction, and finishing affected tasks on their original SDK/agent code. Recommend unique names for new durable runs; same-name agents indistinguishable without hook attributes cannot serialize. Explain that unserializable dataclass context is omitted with a warning; show a serializer/deserializer or `context_override`, and `strict_context=True` to reject omission. |
| `docs/running_agents.md`, `tool_error_formatter`; `docs/tools.md`, "Handling errors in function tools" | Add `tool_exception`, `error`, callback migration, `None` fallback, explicit per-tool precedence, exclusions, and safe model-visible messages. |
| `docs/results.md`, failure recovery and pending input | Explain retained completed outputs, absent custom output metadata after failed extraction, original session ownership, and the terminal-output replay limit. State that completed stop tools can reject added pending input; finish that run before starting a new user turn. |
| `docs/sessions/index.md`, Conversations, Redis, and compaction sections | Document 20-item request batches and partial-append reconciliation. Multi-request writes disable client retries and drain the current request on cancellation; single-request writes retain client behavior. Explain deferred compaction during approvals; standalone Redis atomic replacement, Cluster write restrictions, and application coordination across writers. |
| `docs/mcp.md`, tool discovery and agent-level configuration | Document `FunctionTool.mcp_annotations` as copied optional metadata; absent annotations return `None` and omitted hints remain omitted. Consumers apply the installed MCP defaults. State that metadata neither authorizes execution nor enters model schemas or serialized tool origin. Distinguish MCP failure handlers from the run-wide formatter. |
| `docs/sandbox/clients.md`, local and hosted clients | Optionally note macOS Launch Services denial and document the Vercel >=0.7.0,<0.9 bound. Preserve the existing local-isolation limitations. |

- Publication timing: publish documentation for new behavior after 0.24.0 is available. These documentation gaps do not block the release.

### Key Changes draft

## Key Changes

0.24.0 adds run-wide function error formatting and MCP discovery annotations, and improves recovery, sandbox safety, and tracing. This minor release includes compatibility changes for custom error callbacks and some saved agent graphs. Review the first two highlights before upgrading.

### Highlights:

- **Update custom error formatters.** `RunConfig.tool_error_formatter` can receive `kind="tool_exception"` and an optional `error`. Handle the new kind or return `None` to retain the default message. Explicit per-tool handlers keep precedence; unconfigured defaults stay unchanged.
- **Plan upgrades around saved runs.** New RunState snapshots use schema 1.21. Finish affected older same-name agent graphs on their original SDK. Keep the agent code and original hook ordering unchanged. Use unique agent names for new durable runs; renaming a saved graph is not a migration.
- **Recover completed work more reliably.** Deferred approval history, completed tool outputs, aliases, and compaction state survive supported recovery paths. Automatic compaction waits for approvals. Redis replaces history atomically on supported standalone clients. Conversations appends respect the 20-item request limit. Reconcile partial writes before retrying.
- **Harden local execution and display.** macOS sandbox commands deny Launch Services requests. Sandbox tools recover from invalid model arguments. Protected mount errors preserve caller exception data while detaching the caught traceback. The realtime demo displays tool content as text.
- **Honor tracing choices through resume and cleanup.** Per-run tracing opt-out applies inside caller traces, and approved resumed tools attach to the resumed agent span.
- **Use richer integration examples and metadata.** MCP tools expose optional `mcp_annotations` as discovery hints. New Decisions recipes demonstrate classification, routing, and tool review with OpenAI >=3.26.0,<4. They use a separate client, not an Agents model adapter.
- **Refresh optional dependency locks.** The Temporal extra uses `temporalio==1.34.0`; the Vercel extra supports `vercel-sandbox>=0.7.0,<0.9`. Core Python and OpenAI SDK minimums are unchanged.

Thanks to @masasron for reporting the macOS local sandbox issue fixed in #5335.

### Notes

- This review covers the exact candidate above, including its release metadata. Changes to main, the candidate, or its API baseline require a fresh release check and approval.

repo.readme:
---

The open-source browser agent. Run it locally with any LLM, or on [Browser Use Cloud](https://cloud.browser-use.com): stealth browsers from $0.02/hour, top score (90.5%) on [Stealth Bench V2](https://browser-use.com/benchmarks/browsers).

# Navigate the web like a human does. Find an available slot, pick a date and time, handle the CAPTCHA, and book a driving test. ![Browser Use V4 booking a driving test](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/135885e8-1141-4e10-b719-bf690ae7d260) [Explore more demos and prompts ↗](https://browser-use.com/showcase)
> **AI agents and crawlers:** read [browser-use.com/llms.txt](https://browser-use.com/llms.txt) for the product map (open source, Browser Harness, Cloud browsers, Agents API, pricing) and [docs.browser-use.com/llms.txt](https://docs.browser-use.com/llms.txt) for the documentation index. Browser Use is the open-source browser agent (Python and TypeScript), a $0.02 per browser-hour cloud browser with stealth, CAPTCHA solving and residential proxies, and a hosted agent API. # Which Browser Use do I need? - **[Path 1: Fully Hosted Cloud](#path-1-fully-hosted-cloud):** Scale up with a fully hosted agent and browser. - **[Path 2: CLI](#path-2-cli):** Automate your own browser tasks. - **[Path 3: Python Library](#path-3-python-library):** Run the open source Browser Use agent locally from your own code. # Quickstart ## Path 1: Fully Hosted Cloud Scale browser automation with our hosted agent, stealth browsers, and infrastructure for profiles, recordings, and data policies. [Get started with the API ↗](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/agent/quickstart) New Google, GitHub, or Microsoft signups get **$1 cloud credit**.
## Path 2: CLI Paste this prompt into Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw, or your favorite agent. ```text Install or upgrade browser-use to the latest stable version with uv using Python 3.12, run `browser-use skill install` to register the skill, and connect it to my browser. If setup or connection fails, follow https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md. ```
## Path 3: Python Library Run the Browser Use agent locally from Python, with your choice of model and a local or cloud browser: **1. Install Browser Use (Python >= 3.11):** With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) installed, run `uv init --python 3.12` first if you're starting a new project. ```bash uv add browser-use ``` **2. Add your [OpenAI API key](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys) to `.env`:** ```bash # .env OPENAI_API_KEY=your-key # BROWSER_USE_API_KEY=your-key # Optional: BU2 model or cloud browser ``` For either optional Browser Use service, get a [Browser Use API key](https://cloud.browser-use.com/new-api-key). **3. Save this as `agent.py`:** ```python import asyncio from browser_use import Agent, Browser, ChatBrowserUse, ChatOpenAI from dotenv import load_dotenv load_dotenv() async def main(): llm = ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-5.6-luna', reasoning_effort='xhigh') # llm = ChatBrowserUse(model='bu-2-0') # Use BU2 instead; requires BROWSER_USE_API_KEY agent = Agent( task="Find the number of stars of the browser-use repo", llm=llm, # browser=Browser(use_cloud=True), # Use a cloud browser; requires BROWSER_USE_API_KEY ) history = await agent.run() print(history.final_result()) if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main()) ``` To use BU2, replace the `ChatOpenAI` line with the commented `ChatBrowserUse` line. The cloud-browser option works with either model. **4. Run it:** ```bash uv run agent.py ``` The agent opens a browser, looks up the repository, and prints its answer. **5. Run the same agent on a cloud browser (no Chrome to install; works in Docker, CI, and serverless):** Set `BROWSER_USE_API_KEY` ([get a key](https://cloud.browser-use.com/new-api-key?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme-path3)), then uncomment the `browser=` line in `agent.py` and run it again: ```python agent = Agent( task="Find the number of stars of the browser-use repo", llm=llm, browser=Browser(use_cloud=True), ) ``` Cloud browsers cost $0.02 per browser-hour plus network traffic ([pricing](https://browser-use.com/pricing)), and add stealth, residential proxies, CAPTCHA solving, and a live view URL. Same code, no other changes. [Python library docs ↗](https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/introduction)
# Browser Use toolsets for Claude Maintained by Browser Use. Compatible with Claude. Use Claude's browser toolset with Browser Use as the driver. Browser Use implements all 31 browser actions and can control a local browser, a Browser Use Cloud browser, or an existing remote browser over CDP. Bash is included in the Browser Use integration for processing data and writing files. Requires an Anthropic SDK version that includes `anthropic.tools.browser`. Bash requires a Linux or macOS host with `/bin/bash`; use WSL on Windows. The snippet below runs inside an async function; see the quickstart for a complete script. ```python import os from anthropic import AsyncAnthropic from browser_use.integrations.toolsets_for_claude import Bash, BrowserUse task = 'Open example.com and report its page title.' driver = BrowserUse() # Or BrowserUse(use_cloud=True) bash = Bash(output_dir='outputs') async with driver, AsyncAnthropic() as client: runner = client.beta.messages.tool_runner( model=os.environ['ANTHROPIC_MODEL'], max_tokens=32_768, max_iterations=100, tools=[driver, bash], messages=[{'role': 'user', 'content': task}], ) result = await runner.until_done() ``` [Quickstart ↗](examples/integrations/toolsets-for-claude) · [Integration docs ↗](https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/customize/integrations/toolsets-for-claude)
# Browser Use Benchmark v2 This [very hard benchmark](https://github.com/browser-use/benchmark) targets the hardest browser tasks. On easier tasks, even smaller models can achieve very high success rates. Results shown are from a 60-task subset of BU Bench V2. ## Integrations, hosting, custom tools, MCP, and more on our [Docs ↗](https://docs.browser-use.com)
# FAQ
Should I use the fully hosted cloud, CLI, or Python library? - **[Fully Hosted Cloud](#path-1-fully-hosted-cloud):** Send tasks through the API and let Browser Use run the agent, browser, and infrastructure. - **[CLI](#path-2-cli):** Give an existing agent (Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw, Pi, Cursor, etc.) browser access. You can use it interactively or in scripts. - **[Python Library](#path-3-python-library):** Run the open source agent in your own application, with custom tools, structured output, and your choice of model. The CLI and Python library can each connect to a local or cloud browser. A cloud browser hosts the browser; the fully hosted API runs the agent as well.
What's the best model to use? We recommend **BU2**, our model optimized for browser automation: `ChatBrowserUse(model='bu-2-0')`. It uses `BROWSER_USE_API_KEY`; `ChatBrowserUse()` currently selects the same model. The best choice depends on your tasks, latency, and budget. See the [BU2 model card](https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/bu-2-0-model-card), [benchmark](https://github.com/browser-use/benchmark), and [supported models and pricing](https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/supported-models) to compare options.
Can I use Claude / GPT / Gemini through ChatBrowserUse? Yes. `ChatBrowserUse` accepts provider-prefixed model IDs through the Browser Use gateway, using `BROWSER_USE_API_KEY`: ```python from browser_use import Agent, ChatBrowserUse llm = ChatBrowserUse(model='anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6') # or 'google/gemini-3-pro' agent = Agent(task='...', llm=llm) ``` You can also use providers directly through wrappers such as `ChatOpenAI`, `ChatAnthropic`, and `ChatGoogle`, with each provider's own API key. See [supported models](https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/supported-models).
Do I need to provide a system prompt? No. `Agent(...)` supplies the Browser Use system prompt automatically, including when you change models. Put your task in `task=`. Use `extend_system_message` to add instructions or `override_system_message` to replace the default prompt when you need custom behavior. See the [custom system prompt example](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/examples/features/custom_system_prompt.py).
Can I use custom tools with the agent? Yes. Register a function with `Tools` and pass it to the agent. This example adds a tool for the current UTC time and uses `BROWSER_USE_API_KEY` from `.env`: ```python import asyncio from datetime import datetime, timezone from browser_use import ActionResult, Agent, ChatBrowserUse, Tools from dotenv import load_dotenv load_dotenv() tools = Tools() @tools.action(description='Get the current date and time in UTC.') def get_current_time() -> ActionResult: return ActionResult(extracted_content=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()) async def main(): agent = Agent( task="What is the current UTC time?", llm=ChatBrowserUse(model='bu-2-0'), tools=tools, ) history = await agent.run() print(history.final_result()) if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main()) ```
Can I use this for free? The Python library is free and [MIT-licensed](LICENSE). Model inference and hosted browsers are separate: API providers, including `ChatBrowserUse`, and Browser Use Cloud charge for usage. You can also use a local browser and a local model through [Ollama](https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/supported-models#ollama), subject to your hardware and model requirements.
Terms of Service This open-source library is licensed under the MIT License. For Browser Use services & data policy, see our [Terms of Service](https://browser-use.com/legal/terms-of-service) and [Privacy Policy](https://browser-use.com/privacy/).
How do I handle authentication? - **Local browser:** Use `Browser.from_system_chrome()` to reuse a Chrome profile. See the [real-browser guide](https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/customize/browser/real-browser) and [example](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/examples/browser/real_browser.py). - **Cloud browser:** Follow the [profile sync guide](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/interaction-skills/profile-sync.md), then use `Browser(use_cloud=True, cloud_profile_id='your-profile-id')`. Profile sync transfers cookies, not local storage, IndexedDB, or extensions. Some sites may require you to sign in again.
How do I solve CAPTCHAs? [Browser Use Cloud](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/browser/quickstart) provides stealth browsers and proxies designed to reduce bot detection and CAPTCHA challenges. With the Python library, enable a cloud browser with `Browser(use_cloud=True)` and set `BROWSER_USE_API_KEY`. Results depend on the site and challenge; no browser configuration guarantees that every CAPTCHA can be avoided or solved.
How do I go into production? Choose how much you want to manage: - **Keep your agent code:** Connect the CLI or Python library to [cloud browsers](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/browser/quickstart) for managed browser infrastructure, stealth, profiles, and recordings. - **Have us run the agent too:** Use the [fully hosted Cloud API](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/agent/quickstart) to submit tasks and retrieve results. You can also host the Python library and browsers on your own infrastructure.
Can I rerun a task without calling the model on every step? Yes. Save a successful run, then replay its clicks and typing with new values. The snippet below runs inside an async function: ```python from browser_use import Agent, ChatBrowserUse llm = ChatBrowserUse() agent = Agent(task='Open https://example.com/billing and request an invoice copy for Ada Lovelace, ada@example.com', llm=llm) await agent.run() agent.save_history('invoice_run.json') print(agent.detect_variables()) # names come from the form's fields, e.g. 'name' and 'email' # Later: the same clicks and typing with new values, no model call per step results = await Agent(task='', llm=llm).load_and_rerun( 'invoice_run.json', variables={'name': 'Grace Hopper', 'email': 'grace@example.com'}, skip_failures=False ) ``` - Use the variable names `detect_variables()` prints. An unknown name is skipped with a warning, and the recorded value is typed instead. - Extract steps and the closing summary still call the model. - If the page changed, the replay raises `RuntimeError` at the first step it cannot match. The steps before it already ran, so check whether the form was sent before you run the agent again. - Keep the saved file private. With `sensitive_data`, typed secrets are saved as `key` placeholders, but page snapshots and results are saved as they were and can still contain them. Give the replaying agent the same `sensitive_data`; without it, the placeholder text is typed. [Example](examples/features/rerun_history.py)

## Related Repositories | Repository | What it's for | | --- | --- | | [Browser Harness](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness) | Our CLI for giving AI agents control of your browser. | | [Browser Harness JS](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness-js) | Give your JavaScript agent control of a real browser. | | [Browser Use Pi](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use-pi) | Run a TypeScript browser agent built on Pi. | | [Cloud SDK](https://github.com/browser-use/sdk) | Integrate Browser Use Cloud into your application. | | [Video Use](https://github.com/browser-use/video-use) | Edit videos with your coding agent. | | [macOS Harness](https://github.com/browser-use/macos-harness) | Give your agent control of Mac apps, browsers, and files. | | [Benchmark](https://github.com/browser-use/benchmark) | Explore browser tasks and compare agent performance. |

latestRelease.body:
This release keeps the Python agent and its existing models. The Pi migration remains separate.

Changes since the last PyPI release:
- Add OpenAI browser tools and the shared Bash helper.
- Improve bounded page observations, form state, file access, and browser recovery.
- Fix temporary empty Cloud tab URLs.
- Keep screenshots, crops, and clicks aligned on scaled displays.
- Clean up failed browser reconnect initialization.
- Improve missing-key errors for Cloud browsers.
- Support Browser Use Cloud SDK V4 imports.
- Update aiohttp from 3.14.3 to 3.14.5.
- Refresh Cloud guidance and saved-task replay examples.

Validation:
- GitHub checks pass on the exact release source.
- Pre-commit passes for the version change.
- The wheel and source package build successfully.
- Package metadata and all five CLI entries pass validation.
- All 171 packaged Python files match the existing Python runtime.
- The installed wheel runs `browser-use --help`.

Install with `uv add browser-use==0.13.14` or `pip install browser-use==0.13.14`.

The protected publishing workflow requires another release reviewer. PyPI publication follows that approval.
